newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Florida Panthers aiming for Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Florida Panthers aiming for Wall Street.

text.p: The Florida Panthers hockey team is taking a shot at Wall Street this week as its successful owner Wayne Huizenga takes the team public in a $73 million offering of stock to financial investors and fans.

The Panthers' weak financial record should be outshined by its smashing team record, analysts say, and the Midas touch of Huizenga. He built video chain Blockbuster Entertainment, controls Republic Industries Inc, and owns the Miami Dolphins football team and the Florida Marlins baseball team.
"This deal has lots of sex appeal because of the team and Huizenga, but it's losing money so we'll see how it trades," said Barbara Bradley, managing director of syndicate at Laidlaw Equities Inc.
The Panthers, formed only three years ago, had a 12-game unbeaten streak until last week, and last year went to the Stanley Cup Finals, but lost to the Colorado Avalanche.
"We think this team is several years away from profitability, if at all, so this is a real leap of faith," said the IPO Insider report.

The company has never posted a profit in three years of operation and revenues have been jagged, cut sharply in fiscal 1995 by the hockey strike. For fiscal 1996, which ended in June, the company lost $25 million on revenues of $33 million.
Cash flow is also negative, with a deficit of $55.4 million at June 30, 1996, meaning it could need more capital infusions, according to a regulatory filing.

If investors are willing to ignore the losses, and some are, the hat trick for the Panther's IPO could be the short supply of stock being offered. Parent company Florida Panthers Holdings Inc will offer 4.6 million of the total 7.3 million shares to private investors, leaving only 2.7 million shares for the market to squabble over.
"Given the expected interest and demand by individual fans, we would not be surprised by near-terms gains. Offered at 10, it will reach at least $15," the IPO Insider said.

The Class A shares will be sold at $10 each and will trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol "PUCK." About 60 percent of the company will be sold off, although Huizenga will keep voting control of the Panthers through a second class of stock, per NHL rules.

One critical issue for the team is the completion of its new Broward County Civic Arena in time for the 1998-1999 season. Until it moves out of its current small Miami Arena, the team says it will continue to post yearly losses of at least $20 million. But the company has become embroiled in a lawsuit over the arenas.

Currently the only other publicly traded sports team is the Boston Celtics LP, which trades at about 8 times earnings. There have also been published reports that George Steinbrenner might be considering taking the New York Yankee baseball team to market.

The deal could also do well due to the dearth of strong issues this week despite a heavy calendar. Another issue that could shine is Lehman Brothers' Maginet MGNT.O, which supplies pay-per-view video entertainment and interactive video services to the hotel indsutry outside North America, according to John Fitzpatrick, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.
Twinlab , a Long Island based maker of vitamin and nutritional supplements may also fare well after the company pulled the plug on a summer offering.

"There's lots of smaller deals as everyone scurries to bring deals to market before Thanksgiving while the market's still strong. Twinlab is in much better shape than it was on the first round. They brought in Adams Harkness & Hill and have got a lot of institutional relationships," Bradley said.
"Between now and next week, we'll see lots of deals hit the table and then really slow down at the week of Thanksgiving," she said.
Other companies tentatively slated to go public this week:
-- O'Gara Inc , which makes ballistic and blast protected vehicle armoring systems. The Fairfield, Ohio company plans to offer 3.0 million shares at a maximum price of $10 a share.

-- ProSource Inc plans to offer 3.4 million at $14 to $16 each. The Coral Gables, Fla., company is an independent foodservice distributor to chain restaurants including Burger King, Arby's, Wendy's, and TGI Friday.
-- Introgen Therapeutics The Austin, Texas company develops gene therapy proudcts to treat cancer.
